description:
Radio details for one pass of a satellite over a location: its known downlink (and uplink) frequencies, the Doppler swing, when to tune to what frequency (at 10 and 30 degrees up and closest approach), and a table (at most 40 evenly spaced rows) of time, azimuth, elevation, range and receive frequency for pointing an antenna and tuning a radio.

Uses the next pass above minElevation, or the one peaking nearest `time` (past or future, within 30 days of the orbital elements' epoch). A satellite that never sets here (geosynchronous) gets the next 24 hours instead. Give frequencyMHz to use a frequency other than the default downlink; the default is the most recently heard downlink when SatNOGS heard one, else the catalog's.

Downlinks carry reception from SatNOGS Network observations when known: { state (heard, silent: stations tried and heard nothing, or unknown: no observations, never a sign it is dead), heardLast48h, heardLast7d, heardLast30d, failedLast30d, lastHeard }, listed most recently heard first; receptionSource names the source (CC BY-SA 4.0).

Predictions from published elements: the transmitter's own frequency offset is unknown, so the curve's shape is what to compare.

passUrl opens this pass on seeksat.com on the same frequency, to hand to the user; its Radio chart downloads the full table as CSV. When there is no pass (it never rises above minElevation here, or none within windowHours), window is null and message says why; the downlinks are still listed. To choose a satellite or pass first use find_best_pass with mode radio, or find_passes; for a sky chart of the pass use get_pass_chart.

frequencyMHz.description: the downlink to compute Doppler for, in MHz. Default: the satellite's default known downlink.

lat.description: observer latitude in decimal degrees, north positive (-90 to 90). Give it with lon, or give location instead.

location.description: where the observer is, when lat and lon are not given (they win when both are): a Maidenhead grid square (EN52, EN52ve, EN52ve12), coordinates in any common form ("41.88, -87.63", "41.88N 87.63W", "41°52'48"N 87°37'48"W", a Google Maps link or geo: URI), all read locally, or a place name (city, address, landmark) looked up with OpenStreetMap. Prefer lat and lon, or a grid square, when you have them: a place name is a network lookup.

lon.description: observer longitude in decimal degrees, east positive and west negative (-180 to 180).

minElev.description: old name for minElevation; still accepted.

minElevation.description: lowest elevation that counts: a pass must climb above it, and rise and set are when it crosses it, in degrees above the horizon (0 to 90). Default 10.

minElevationDeg.description: old name for minElevation; still accepted.

passTime.description: old name for time; still accepted.

satellite.description: NORAD catalog number (as a number or a string) or a name, e.g. 25544, "25544" or "iss". e.g. "so-50" or 27607.

time.description: a time near the wanted pass's peak (e.g. from find_passes), past or future. Default: the next pass. ISO 8601 with Z or an offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00:00-06:00"; a time with no offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00", is read in the observer's time zone, and the result echoes how it was read (interpretedAs). A local time the clocks skip at a daylight-saving change is moved forward, with a note.

windowHours.description: how far ahead to look, in hours, up to 240 (10 days). Default 48. How far past the start to look for a pass.

name: get_radio_pass
title: Radio pass details
